today.h: Huang's Return: S&P +4.73% and Nasdaq +6.51%, the Best Day Since April 2025
today.d: Nvidia's board put Jensen Huang back 11 days after he resigned and the AI complex re-rated: NVDA +31.48%, the Nasdaq +6.51%, the VIX -25.83%. The S&P is still 7.44% below its record, the equal-weight index lagged by 2.12 points, and energy fell as crude hit a three-month low.
today.c1: Nvidia put its founder back and the AI complex re-rated. The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17 (+326.78 points) and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% to 24,089.56 (+1,471.83), the best day for both since April 2025; the Dow added 3.01% to 49,595.31 (+1,447.98). Nvidia jumped 31.48% to $165.05 after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, 11 days after he resigned, adding back nearly $1 trillion of market value in its best day since May 2003. The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 14.03%. The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62. Nine of 11 sectors rose, led by technology at +8.97%; energy -1.06% and staples -0.09% were the only decliners. The S&P is still 7.44% below its 10/6 record of 7,818.93.
today.c4:
• The trigger: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO effective immediately on 11/23, 11 days after his resignation; it said it had input from senior levels of the US government and that the move poses no national security risk.
  • The tape: NVDA +31.48% to $165.05, its best day since May 2003, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index +14.03%; Micron +19.04% and Dell +20.46% were among the largest supply-chain gains.
  • The caveat: the S&P is still 7.44% below its 10/6 record and the rally recovered only about $3 trillion of the $8 trillion lost since that peak.
  • The rate backdrop: the 10Y closed unchanged at 4.92% and a 25bp December hike is still the priced outcome, with a 50bp move largely priced out.
  • The gate: October PCE prices on 11/25; US markets are closed 11/26 for Thanksgiving and close early at 1 p.m. ET on 11/27.

chains.t: ① The Board Put the Founder Back and the AI Trade Re-Rated
steps: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The board said it had input from senior levels of the US government and that the reinstatement poses no national security risk; Trump said he spoke with the board and "convinced" them.
NVDA rose 31.48% to $165.05, its best day since May 2003, adding back nearly $1 trillion in market capitalization.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 14.03% to 9,588.05, while Micron +19.04% and Dell +20.46% were among the largest gains.
The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% to 24,089.56, their best sessions since April 2025; the Dow added 3.01%.
The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62, ending the S&P's seven-session losing streak.
chains.d: The AI trade's discount was a governance discount; removing it produced the biggest one-day rally since April 2025 and cut the S&P's distance from its record from 11.62% to 7.44%.

news.fact: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, and said it had input from senior levels of the US government and that the move poses no national security risk.
President Trump told CNBC he spoke with Nvidia's board and "convinced" them to reinstate Huang, and that Huang "did nothing wrong".
Nvidia rose 31.48% to $165.05, its best day since May 2003, gaining back nearly $1 trillion in market capitalization.
Micron rose 19.04%, Dell 20.46% and AMD 6.85%.
The S&P 500 added 4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% to 24,089.56, both their best daily performances since April 2025; the Dow gained 1,447.98 points, or 3.01%, to 49,595.31.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) closed at 9,588.05, up 14.03% from 8,408.59.
The VIX closed at 26.62, down 25.83% from 35.89.

chains.t: ③ Oil Fell on Supply, Not on Demand
steps: Brent for January settled down $3.20, or 3.46%, at $89.37 a barrel, its lowest since August 31.
WTI for January settled down $3.24, or 3.88%, at $80.17, its lowest since August 10.
Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened and crude began flowing into storage at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the National Oil Corp chairman told Reuters.
Rising Middle East supplies offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region; energy was the worst sector.
The energy ETF (XLE) closed at $59.87, down 1.06%, the only sector fund more than 1% lower.
chains.d: Oil's 3.5-3.9% slide was a supply story, a Libyan pipeline restart and heavier Middle East exports, which is why energy was the only sector down more than 1% on a risk-on day.
